abstract.p: An amplifier comprises inputs (INN, INI) for receiving a differential input signal (Vin) and outputs (CO6, CQ7) for delivering a differential intermediate signal; an intermediate stage (INTst) for converting the differential intermediate signal to a non-differential intermediate signal and comprises a current mirror (Q5R5Q4R4) having an input branch (Q5R5) and an output branch (Q4R4); an output stage (OPst) coupled to the output branch (Q4R4) and an output (OP) for delivering an output signal (Vout); and means for stabilizing the amplifier comprising a capacitor (Cm2) coupled between the output (OP) and the input branch (Q5R5). Thus, the current mirror (Q5R5Q4R4) is also used for signal inversion within a respective Miller loop. Thus, no current mirror is needed in the output stage (OPst) for the purpose of stabilizing the respective Miller loop. As a result the bandwidth of the amplifier is extended. The above-mentioned measures provide a large bandwidth and low supply voltage amplifier.

Un amplificateur comporte les éléments suivants : entrées (INN, INI) destinées à recevoir un signal d'entrée différentiel (Vin) et, des sorties (CO6, CQ7) étudiées pour fournir un signal différentiel intermédiaire ; étage intermédiaire (INTst) assurant la conversion du signal différentiel intermédiaire en un signal intermédiaire non-différentiel et comprenant un miroir de courant (Q5R5Q4R4) doté d'une branche d'entrée (Q5R5) et d'une branche de sortie (Q4R4) ; un étage de sortie (OPst)couplé à la branche de sortie (Q4R4) et une sortie (OP) fournissant un signal de sortie (Vout) ; et des dispositifs de stabilisation de l'amplificateur comprenant un condensateur (Cm2) monté entre la sortie (OP) et la branche d'entrée (Q5R5). Ainsi, le miroir de courant (Q5R5Q4R4) sert également à inverser le signal dans la boucle de Miller correspondante. Dans le même ordre d'idée, aucun miroir de courant n'est nécessaire au niveau de l'étage de sortie (OPst) pour stabiliser la boucle de Miller correspondante. Ce système procure un élargissement de la bande de l'amplificateur. Grâce aux procédés susmentionnés, on dispose d'un amplificateur à large bande et à faible tension d'alimentation.

description.p: Amplifier with stabilization means.

The invention relates to an amplifier comprising an input stage having a pair of inputs for receiving a differential input signal and a pair of outputs for delivering a differential intermediate signal in response to the differential input signal; an intermediate stage for converting the differential intermediate signal to a non-differential intermediate signal, which intermediate stage comprises a current mirror having an input branch and an output branch for receiving the differential intermediate signal; an output stage having an input coupled to the output branch and having an output for delivering an output signal to an output of the amplifier; and means for stabilizing the amplifier.

Such an amplifier is known from the general state of the art as shown in Figure 1. The known amplifier has a first reference terminal VEE and a second reference terminal Vcc- A supply voltage source SV for biasing the amplifier is connected between the first reference terminal VEE and the second reference terminal Vcc- The known amplifier further comprises an input stage IPST, an intermediate stage INTST, and an output stage OPST- The input stage IPST comprises a transistor Q6 and a transistor Q7> which are arranged as a differential pair. The bases of the transistors Q6 and Q7 are connected to a pair of inputs INNJNI to which a differential input signal V;n is supplied. The emitters of the transistors Q6 and Q7 are connected to a current source I6 for biasing the differential pair. The differential pair delivers a differential intermediate signal at the collectors CQ6 and CQ7 of the transistors Q6 and Q7, respectively. The intermediate stage INTST has an input branch comprising a series arrangement of a resistor R5 and a transistor Q5. The transistor Q5 is arranged as a diode. The intermediate stage INTST further has an output branch comprising a series arrangement of a resistor R4 and a transistor Q . The base of the transistor Q is connected to the base of transistor Q5. The input branch and the output branch are coupled between the first reference terminal VEE and the second reference terminal Vcc- The input branch and the output branch are biased by current sources I5 and Lt, respectively. The output stage OPST comprises a transistor Q2 having a base coupled to the collector of transistor Q , an emitter coupled to the first reference terminal VEE, and a collector coupled to the input of a current mirror Q3,Qπ. The input of the current mirror Q3,Qι3 is formed by a diode-connected transistor Q3. The output of the current mirror Q3,Qι3 is formed by the collector of the transistor Q13. The base
and emitter of the transistor Qι3 are coupled to the base and the emitter of the transistor Q3, respectively. The transistor Qι3 is biased by a current source I3. The output stage OPST further comprises a transistor Qi, which is biased by a current source Ii. A base of the transistor Qi is coupled to the collector of the transistor Q13. A collector of the transistor Qi is coupled to the output OP of the amplifier to deliver an output signal Vout. An emitter of transistor Q is coupled to the first reference terminal VEE- Miller capacitors CM I and CM for stabilizing the amplifier are coupled between the output OP and the base of transistor Qi, and between the output OP and the base of transistor Q2, respectively.

The principle of operation of the known amplifier as shown in Figure 1 is as follows. The differential pair Q6,Q7 converts the differential input signal Vin into currents of opposite phases, which are delivered by the collectors CQ6 and CQ7. The intermediate stage INTST converts these currents into a single current, which is delivered by the collector of transistor Q . This single current is then amplified and converted by the output stage OPST in order to deliver the output signal Vout of the amplifier. In order to obtain a stable amplifier, the amplifier may include only one gain-stage with a so-called dominant pole and it may further include stages with non-dominant poles. If the Miller capacitors CMI and CM2 are disregarded then the amplifier comprises in fact three gain stages, each with a dominant pole. The input stage IPST and the intermediate stage INTST form together a first gain stage with a first dominant pole at the collector of the transistor Q4. The transistor Q2 and the current mirror Q3,Qι3 form together a second gain stage with a second dominant pole at the collector of transistor Q]3. The transistor Qi is a third gain stage with a third dominant pole at the output OP. The Miller capacitor CM I performs pole splitting, i.e. the third dominant pole becomes non-dominant while the second dominant pole becomes even more dominant. The Miller capacitor CM also performs pole splitting, i.e. the first dominant pole becomes even more dominant while the second dominant pole becomes, in comparison with the first dominant pole, non-dominant. Thus, the amplifier has only one dominant pole at the collector of transistor Q . Therefore, the components of the amplifier can be dimensioned quite easily in order to obtain a stable operation of the amplifier. The Miller compensation technique for stabilizing the amplifier in the manner as shown in Figure 1 is known as the nested Miller compensation technique since it comprises a first Miller loop formed by the transistor Qi and the Miller capacitor CM I , and a second Miller loop formed by the transistor Q2, the current mirror Q3,Qι3, and the first Miller loop. Thus, the first Miller loop is nested within the second Miller loop. The function of the current mirror Q3,Qι3 is to obtain a correct phase relationship within the second Miller loop.
A problem of the known amplifier is that the current mirror Q3,Qι3 must handle a relatively large base current of transistor Qj and therefore the transistors Q3 and Qι3 must have relatively large dimensions. In the quiescent state of the amplifier the current mirror Q3,Qι3 is biased by a relatively small current so that the transit frequency of the current mirror Q3,Qi3 is relatively low, which adversely influences the maximum bandwidth of the amplifier. It is an object of the invention to provide an improved amplifier with an extended bandwidth.

To this end, according to the invention, the amplifier of the type defined in the opening paragraph is characterized in that the means for stabilizing the amplifier include a capacitor coupled between the output of the amplifier and the input branch.

The invention is based on the insight that the current mirror already available within the intermediate stage LNTST can also be used in a respective Miller loop to stabilize the amplifier as an alternative to the above-mentioned second Miller loop without causing a wrong phase relationship in the respective Miller loop. As a consequence, the current mirror Q3,Qι3 is not necessary in the respective Miller loop. Therefore, the maximum bandwidth of the amplifier is extended.

In the general state of the art another solution is known for the above-mentioned problem caused by the current mirror Q3,Qι3. The solution is the use of a differential stage in the output stage OPST instead of the transistor Q2 and the current mirror Q3,Qι3. This solution, however, causes another problem: the differential stage cannot function properly at a low supply voltage. The amplifier according to the invention does not have a differential stage in the output stage OPST- Therefore, the amplifier according to the invention has a large bandwidth and can also function properly at a low supply voltage.
Further advantageous embodiments of the inventions are specified in Claims 2 - 8.

Figure 2 shows a circuit diagram of a first embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. An important difference with the circuit of Figure 1 is that the Miller capacitor CM2 is connected to the input branch Q5,R5 of the intermediate stage INTST instead of to the base of the transistor Q2. As a consequence the current mirror Q3,Qι3 in the known circuit of Figure 1 is not necessary in the circuit of Figure 2. Therefore, the collector of the transistor Q is connected to the base of transistor Qi. Thus, the intermediate stage INTST has a double function: converting the differential intermediate signal from the collectors CQ6 and CQ7 into a non-differential signal at the collector of transistor Q4, and functioning as a
current mirror in a respective Miller loop with regard to the capacitor CM2- The connection of the Miller capacitor CM2 to the input branch Q5,R5 is, by way of example, made by connecting the Miller capacitor CM2 to the base and the collector of the transistor Q5. As an alternative, the capacitor CM2 can be connected to the emitter of the transistor Q5. Although the Miller capacitor CM2 creates a well defined dominant pole, the two non-dominant poles turn out to be complex, which might reduce the stability of the amplifier. This is caused by the fact that there is no capacitor connected to the base of transistor Q2. Therefore, the base of transistor Q2 is uncontrolled for high frequencies. The stability of the amplifier can be further improved if a capacitor CM3 is arranged in parallel with the output branch Q4,R4. By way of example, the capacitor CM3 is connected between the base of the transistor Q2 and the first reference terminal VEE- Since normally the first and the second reference terminal VEE,Vcc are decoupled, at least for high frequencies, the capacitor CM3 may also be connected between the base of the transistor Q and the second reference terminal Vcc- By the aforementioned decoupling the capacitor CM3 is then also arranged in parallel with the output branch Q4,R4. The capacitor CM3 slightly reduces the bandwidth of the amplifier, but this reduction can, at least partly, be avoided by inserting a resistor in series with the capacitor CM3- The value of the capacitor CM3 is not critical and must only be sufficient to avoid complex poles. The value of the capacitor CM3 need not be matched to other capacitors. For this reason the capacitor CM3 can be formed by a low-quality and compact capacitor such as a junction capacitor.

Figure 3 shows a circuit diagram of a second embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. In comparison with the circuit of Figure 2 the following components have been added: transistors Qι6, Qπ, Q15, and Qι4; resistors Rj5 and Rι4; and current sources I]6 and I15. These components are connected together in a manner similar to the transistors Q6, Q7, Q5, and Q4; the resistors R5 and R4; and the current sources I6 and I5. The elements of the following pairs have a mutually similar operation: Qι6,Q6; Qπ,Q7; Qι5,Q5; Qi4,Q4; Rι5,R5; Ru,R4; Iι6,I6; Iis s- The bases of the transistors Qι6 and Q,7 are, respectively, connected to the inverting input INI and the non-inverting input INN. The collector of transistor Qι4 is connected to the base of transistor Qj. The function of the addition of the above-mentioned components is to form a low-gain and high-frequency path between the inputs LNI,INN and the input of the output stage Q . This has the advantageous effect that the bandwidth of the amplifier is further enhanced significantly without the stability of the amplifier being reduced.
In order to obtain a higher low-frequency gain of the amplifier extra gain stages can be used in the output stage OPST- Naturally, also extra Miller capacitors are needed to stabilize the amplifier. In the known amplifier as shown in Figure 1 the current mirror Q3,Qι3 can be replaced by a so called common emitter stage (or a common source stage) because like the current mirror Q3,Q 3 a common emitter stage also inverts the phase of a signal applied to it. Then there is no need to connect the capacitor CM2 to the input branch Q5,R5. However, if it is desired to use an even number of extra gain stages instead of an odd number of extra gain stages, the current mirror Q3,Qι3 cannot be removed because otherwise the phase relationship in the respective Miller loops would not be correct. However, the use of an amplifier according to the invention enables an even number of gain stages to be used without the current mirror Q3,Q13 being needed.

An example of an even number of extra gain stages in the amplifier according to the invention is shown in Figure 4. In this example two extra (common emitter) gain stages are used: a transistor QEχι biased by a current source IEχι, and a transistor QEχ biased by a current source IEχ . Also two extra capacitors CEχι and CEX2 are added in order to stabilize the amplifier. The capacitor CEχι is connected between the base and the collector of the transistor QEXI, and the capacitor CEχ2 is connected between the output OP and the base of the transistor
QEXI -

Figure 5 shows a circuit diagram of a fourth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a variant of the circuit as shown in Figure 2. The amplifier has a so called rail-to-rail output stage formed by the transistor Qi and a transistor Qioo. The amplifier further comprises a mesh formed by transistors Q203, Q204, Q204ι, and Q203i. The mesh drives the transistors Q2 and Qι03 with signals injected by transistors Q4 and Q7. The mesh can be controlled at the base of transistor Q2031 by a control voltage VAB in order to obtain a feedback class AB biasing of the transistors Qi and Qioo- Capacitors CMIA and CM3A are added in order to stabilize the amplifier. Capacitor CM I A is connected between the output OP and the base of the transistor QJOO, while the capacitor CM3A is connected between the base and the emitter of the transistor Q o3.

Figure 6 shows a circuit diagram of a fifth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a variant of the circuit as shown in Figure 5, i.e. that the amplifier has been provided with a class AB control circuit for supplying the control voltage VAB- The class AB control circuit is formed by transistors Quo, Qiπ, Q112, Q113, Qιi4, and Qn5, which drive the mesh. The transistor Qπo measures, in an indirect way, the current through the transistor Qioo and generates a voltage across a resistor Rπ4. The
current of the transistor Qi is measured by the transistor Qm and is mirrored by the current mirror Qn3,Qn5, which as a consequence generates a voltage across a resistor Rn2- The diode- connected transistors Qn2 and Qπ , form a selector for selecting the lower of the two voltages across the resistors R112 and Rπ4. The control voltage VAB is thus derived from the lower of the two voltages across the resistors R112 and Rn . Transistors Q2o3 and Q203ι form a class AB amplifier and create a class AB feedback loop by controlling the bases of the transistors Q103 and Q2, which drive the transistors Qi and Qι00. The voltage difference between the bases of the transistors Q203 and Q203ι is regulated to virtually zero. As a consequence, the control voltage VAB is equal to a reference voltage VREF across the series arrangement of a diode- connected transistor Q2ι9 and a resistor R2!9. Since the transistor Q2J9 and the resistor R2]9 are biased by a current source I2j , the reference voltage VREF, and as a consequence the control voltage VAB, is determined by the current delivered by the current source I2ι9. The transistors Qi and Qioo are controlled in such a way that they are biased with at least a certain minimum current. A feed forward path is used to stabilize the class AB feedback loop. The feed forward path is obtained by the use of a feed forward amplifier Q2ι3,Q2ι3ι, which drives the transistors Qi and Qioo via current mirrors Q2ι6ι,Q2ι63 and Q2i60,Q2i62-

Figure 7 shows a circuit diagram of a sixth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a variant of the circuit as shown in Figure 6. In a manner similar to and for the same reason as stated with reference to in Figure 3, a feed forward path, created by the transistors Q]6 and Qπ, is added. The output signals of the feed forward input stage Qι6, Qπ are combined by a summing circuit formed by transistors Q2ι5 and Q2π and resistors R2ι5 and R2ι7. The output current of the summing circuit is delivered by the transistors Q ]7 and Qπ and flows through the transistors Q2ι3 and Q2131 and is used to drive the transistors Qi and Qioo via the current mirrors Q ι6ι,Q2ι63 and Q2ι6o,Q2i62- Figure 8 shows a circuit diagram of a seventh embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a so called BiCMOS version of the embodiment as shown in Figure 7. The use of bipolar transistors and CMOS transistors gives the advantages of a high gain, a high bandwidth, a low input offset, and a high output current capability at the output OP. Though the resistors R5, R , R ι5, and R2[7 as indicated in Figure 7 are not necessary in the embodiment shown in Figure 8 they may also be included in the embodiment shown in Figure 8.

Figures 9 and 10 show circuit diagrams of an eight and a ninth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. The topologies of these circuits are almost the same as
those of the previously discussed circuits. However, an alternative for the class AB control circuit is provided by the arrangement of transistors Quo - Q115-

Figure 11 shows a circuit diagram of a tenth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. In this embodiment NPN transistors are combined with PMOS transistors. With this embodiment a very powerful circuit is obtained in BiCMOS technology. NPN transistors have usually a much better performance than PNP transistors. NPN transistors can handle much higher currents, have a higher current gain, and have a much higher transit frequency. PMOS transistors are the best complementary devices and also have a better performance than PNP transistors. The transistors Qi and Qι00 form a so called all-NPN output stage. The NPN transistor Qi is driven by a PMOS transistor Q103, while the NPN transistor Qioo is driven by the PMOS transistor Q . The PMOS transistors Q2 and Qι03 are driven by the PNP transistors Q7 and Q6 of the input stage LPST, via NPN cascode transistors Q20ι and Q2o3. Since the NPN transistor Qioo is arranged as a so called emitter follower, it does not invert signals. As a consequence, the combination of the PMOS transistor Q2 and the NPN transistor Qioo can be stabilized in conventional manners. The combination of the PMOS transistor Qι03 and NPN transistor Qi consists of two inverting stages and can therefore not be stabilized in a conventional way. It is therefore stabilized by capacitors CMI and C 2- The capacitor CMI is connected between the output OP and the base of the NPN transistor Qi. The capacitor CM2 is connected between the output OP and the gate of the PMOS transistor Q103 via the current mirror formed by the NMOS transistors Q5 and Q207 and the NPN transistors Q22ι and Q203- A feed forward path is created using NPN transistors Qι and Qπ of the input stage LPST in order to further extend the bandwidth of the amplifier.
Figure 12 shows a circuit diagram of an eleventh embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a variant of the embodiment as shown in

Figure 11. A class AB control circuit is added comprising NPN transistors Quo - Qns in order to correctly bias the NPN transistors Qi and Qioo- A feed forward path for the class AB feedback loop is created by a PMOS transistor Q2ιo and a current mirror comprising NPN transistors Q 3ι, Q2n, and Q2]3, which current mirror directly drives the transistors Qi and Qioo- Figure 13 shows a circuit diagram of a twelfth embodiment of an amplifier according to the invention. This embodiment is a variant of the circuits as shown in Figures 9 and 10. An important difference is that the current mirrors Q2i6o,Q2i62 and Q2i6i,Q2iό3 are formed by means of NMOS transistors instead of PMOS transistors. By so doing a so called folded structure is obtained. This has the advantage that the amplifier can operate on an even
lower supply voltage. A supply voltage equal to one gate-source voltage plus one saturation voltage is then sufficient.
Figure 14 shows a circuit diagram of an amplifier which has been modified with respect to the circuit diagram of Figure 13. The current mirrors Q2ι6o,Q2i62 and
Q216ι,Q2ι63 are now used not only by the feed forward path of the class AB control loop but also by the signals injected by the transistors Q2 and Q103.

An amplifier comprising an input stage (LPST) having a pair of inputs (LNN,LNI) for receiving a differential input signal (V,n) and a pair of outputs (CQ6,CQ ) for delivering a differential intermediate signal in response to the differential input signal (V;n); an intermediate stage (LNTST) for converting the differential intermediate signal to a non- differential intermediate signal, which intermediate stage (LNTSτ) comprises a current mirror (Q ,R5,Q4,R4) having an input branch (Q5,R5) and an output branch (Q4,R4) for receiving the differential intermediate signal; an output stage (OPST) having an input coupled to the output branch (Q4,R ) and having an output for delivering an output signal (Vout) to an output (OP) of the amplifier; and means for stabilizing the amplifier, characterized in that the means for stabilizing the amplifier includes a capacitor (CM2) coupled between the output (OP) of the amplifier and the input branch (Q5,R5).

2. An amplifier as claimed in Claim 1, characterized in that the means for stabilizing the amplifier include a further capacitor (CM I) coupled between the output (OP) of the amplifier and the input of the output stage (OPSτ).
3. An amplifier as claimed in claim 1 or 2, characterized in that the means for stabilizing the amplifier includes a still further capacitor (CM3) arranged in parallel with the output branch (Q ,R ).

4. An amplifier as claimed in Claim 1, 2, or 3, characterized in that the input branch (Q5,R ) comprises a first transistor (Q5) having a first main electrode, a second main electrode, and a control electrode coupled to the first main electrode; and a first resistor (R5) coupled in series with the second main electrode and a first reference terminal (VEE), and in that the capacitor (CM2) is coupled between the output (OP) of the amplifier and the first main electrode of the first transistor (Q5), and in that the output branch (Q4,R4) comprises a second transistor (Q ) having a first main electrode for delivering the non-differential intermediate signal, a second main electrode, and a control electrode coupled to the control electrode of the
first transistor (Q5); and a second resistor (R ) coupled in series with the second main electrode of the second transistor (Q4) and the first reference terminal (VEE).

5. An amplifier as claimed in Claim 4, characterized in that the capacitor (CM2) is coupled to the second main electrode of the first transistor (Q5) instead of to the first main electrode of the first transistor (Q5).

6. An amplifier as claimed in Claim 4 or 5, characterized in that it comprises first and second cascode transistors (Q201, Q203) arranged in series with the first main electrodes of the first and second transistors (Q5, Q4), respectively.

7. An amplifier as claimed in Claim 4, 5, or 6, characterized in that the output stage (OPST) comprises a first output transistor (Q having a first main electrode coupled to the output (OP) of the amplifier, a second main electrode coupled to the first reference terminal (VEE), and a control electrode;
